```{r}
library(pgmcompR)
```

A dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) describes a process over discrete time by a
two slice template: an initial model for $t = 1$ and a transition model for
$X_t$ given $X_{t-1}$, repeated as often as needed.

## A hidden Markov model

The umbrella world of Russell and Norvig: rain is hidden, umbrellas are
observed.

```{r}
h <- hmm(hidden_states = c("rain", "dry"),
         observation_states = c("umbrella", "none"),
         initial = c(0.5, 0.5),
         transition = matrix(c(0.7, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7), 2),
         emission = matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.2, 0.8), 2))
h
obs <- data.frame(Observation = c("umbrella", "umbrella", "none", "umbrella", "umbrella"))
```

Each column of `transition` is $P(X_t \mid X_{t-1})$ for one previous state.

### Filtering, smoothing, decoding and forecasting

```{r}
filt <- filter_dbn(h, obs)
sapply(filt$marginals, function(m) factor_values(m$Hidden)[1])
filt$loglik
smth <- smooth_dbn(h, obs)
sapply(smth$marginals, function(m) factor_values(m$Hidden)[1])
viterbi_dbn(h, obs)
forecast_dbn(h, obs, horizon = 3)[[3]]$Hidden
```

Filtering uses the evidence up to time $t$; smoothing uses all of it, so the
third day (no umbrella) is less certainly dry after smoothing. Missing
observations (`NA`) are skipped.

## A general DBN

Variables within a slice can depend on each other, and arcs between slices
can connect different variables.

```{r}
st <- list(Health = c("good", "poor"), Exercise = c("no", "yes"), Fatigue = c("no", "yes"))
dbn <- dynamic_bn(st, intra = list(c("Health", "Fatigue"), c("Exercise", "Fatigue")),
                  inter = list(c("Health", "Health"), c("Exercise", "Health"), c("Exercise", "Exercise")))
dbn_parents(dbn, "Health", "transition")
dbn <- add_dbn_cpd(dbn, "Health", c(good = 0.8, poor = 0.2), "initial")
dbn <- add_dbn_cpd(dbn, "Exercise", c(no = 0.6, yes = 0.4), "initial")
fat <- c(0.9, 0.1, 0.7, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5)
dbn <- add_dbn_cpd(dbn, "Fatigue", fat, "initial")
dbn <- add_dbn_cpd(dbn, "Fatigue", fat, "transition")
dbn <- add_dbn_cpd(dbn, "Exercise", c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), "transition")
dbn <- add_dbn_cpd(dbn, "Health", c(0.9, 0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 0.97, 0.03, 0.6, 0.4), "transition")
check_model(dbn)
ev <- data.frame(Fatigue = c("yes", "yes", "no", "no"), Exercise = c(NA, "yes", "yes", NA))
smooth_dbn(dbn, ev)$marginals[[2]]$Health
```

### Simulation and learning

```{r}
sim <- simulate_dbn(dbn, 2000, seed = 1)
head(sim)
learned <- fit_dbn(dbn, sim)
learned$transition$Exercise
```

### Particle filtering

When the joint state of a slice is too large for exact filtering, a
bootstrap particle filter gives approximate filtered marginals:

```{r}
pf <- particle_filter(dbn, ev, n_particles = 5000, seed = 1)
pf$marginals[[4]]$Health
filter_dbn(dbn, ev)$marginals[[4]]$Health
```

## Linear Gaussian state space models

For continuous states with linear dynamics and Gaussian noise, the Kalman
filter and the Rauch Tung Striebel smoother are exact.

```{r}
set.seed(2)
x <- cumsum(rnorm(30, 0, 0.5))
y <- x + rnorm(30, 0, 1)
y[c(10, 11, 20)] <- NA
kf <- kalman_filter(y, A = 1, C = 1, Q = 0.25, R = 1, m0 = 0, P0 = 10)
ks <- kalman_smoother(kf)
plot(y, pch = 16, col = "grey50", ylab = "level", xlab = "time")
lines(x, lwd = 2)
lines(kf$m[, 1], col = "#F2A93B", lwd = 2)
lines(ks$m_smooth[, 1], col = "#3B5BDB", lwd = 2)
legend("topleft", c("truth", "filtered", "smoothed"), col = c("black", "#F2A93B", "#3B5BDB"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```
